chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of the Dhuhr prayer during the heat of summer, but he did not answer me. Later, he said to Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Hilal, 'Zurarah asked me about the time of the Dhuhr prayer during the heat of summer, and I did not inform him, so I felt concerned about that. So convey my greetings to him and tell him: When your shadow is equal to your height, pray Dhuhr, and when your shadow is twice your height, pray Asr.'
And that which indicates that these times are specific to one who prays the voluntary prayers.
ai.seo_question: What is the shadow-based method for determining the time of Dhuhr and Asr prayers during summer heat?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific timing for Dhuhr and Asr during the intense heat of summer (al-Qayz) using shadow length as the primary indicator, a ruling derived from the principle of facilitating worship during extreme conditions. The narration highlights the scholarly practice of delayed response, where the Imam withheld the answer initially to ensure precision or due to the specific context of the questioner, Zarara. The concluding note distinguishes this shadow-based measurement as particularly relevant for voluntary (Nawafil) prayers, reflecting the nuanced juristic distinctions in Shia fiqh regarding prayer times.
